title_en: Describe the scene in specific detail
content_en: Be hyper-specific: describe the scene in rich detail. The more detail the prompt provides, the more control it gives and the closer the image is to what is intended.
applies_when_en: The prompt is short or generic (only the object or genre is named, with no subject appearance, action, place, light or shot size) while the task needs a specific look and control over the result; the result comes out wrong or different every time.
not_applies_when_en: Deliberate freedom for the model is wanted (an open prompt for variety); one prompt pipeline serves many different inputs, where extra specificity breaks the general case; the model is meant to fill in the scene itself from a simple concept or world knowledge; editing a finished image (only the change is described); a product with personal context (Personal Intelligence), where the app supplies the details.
caveats_en: The models respond effectively and efficiently to even the most detailed prompts; long detailed prompts are supported. (models: pro, nb2, lite)
Simple prompts still work; achieving professional results requires more specific instructions. (models: pro)
Instead of specific, lengthy prompts, simple conversational instructions can be given; this is a possibility, not a ban on detail. (models: nb25)

In a restoration pipeline the prompt is generic enough to cover most use cases but also specific enough; a generic instruction ("clean up all physical artifacts") can be made more specific to remove more or fewer artifacts. (models: nb25)
nb25: an under-specified key-value prompt is not fully stable and can generate less optimal results; it benefits from being more precise. (models: unspecified)
What is described precisely (or visible in references) stays stable across runs; under-described parts vary. (models: lite)
Be specific about the subject: who or what is in the image. (models: pro)
Specificity covers three axes: concrete details on subject, lighting, and composition. (models: pro, nb2)

In the Gemini app the benefit is framed as instruction-following accuracy: prompts include as many specifics as can be thought of; the more details, the better the instructions are followed. (models: nb2)

For the first request in the Gemini app (nb25): type a detailed description of the image; the more specific and descriptive the prompt, the closer the result is to what is envisioned. (models: unspecified)
Specificity is demanded repeatedly: be specific, give more specific instructions, clearly state the text, clearly define the role of each reference. (models: pro)
General Gemini advice (the more detail the prompt has, the better; clear and specific instructions) is not directly tied to image generation; for images it applies by extension. (models: unspecified)

title_en: Describe the scene narratively, not keywords
content_en: Describe the scene as a narrative, descriptive paragraph rather than a list of keywords: a narrative paragraph almost always produces a better, more coherent image than a list of disconnected words. When starting from a blank canvas, the prompt author is the director and describes the scene narratively.
applies_when_en: A from-scratch generation prompt (no references) is written as a comma-separated list of words or a set of tags; the task requires an expressive, directed scene.
not_applies_when_en: Short edit commands on an attached or finished image ('Translate to French') and service lines (format, background), which do not need narrative; product fields (NotebookLM, Photos templates) where the prompt is a setting; generation from references, where the key is the role of each reference.
caveats_en: Called "one fundamental principle"; the wording is cautious: "almost always". (models: nb25)
Framed as directing: "stop typing keywords and start directing the scene" (prompt like a creative director). (models: pro, nb2)
Mechanism: the model's core strength is deep language understanding that captures the nuance of prompts. (models: pro, nb2, lite, nb25)
The six prompt templates are themselves full descriptive sentences with slots, not keyword lists. (models: nb25)
Official lite notebook examples use one or two full sentences followed by a comma-separated tail of style/technique descriptors ending with a plain background. (models: lite)

The idea "stop typing keywords and start directing the scene" is repeated; specificity comes through professional vocabulary: lighting, camera/lens, color grading/film stock, materials. (models: pro, nb2)

Writing a great prompt requires both telling a succinct story and painting an elaborate tableau with words; aspect ratio is named as part of the prompt text (Asset Studio), with nothing said about the API parameter. (models: pro)
The NB2 Lite comparison prompts are long narrative paragraphs (about 150-200 words) without keyword lists, weights or parameters; the same prompts are used for NB2 and NB2 Lite. (models: nb2, lite)

When starting with a blank canvas the author is the director: a simple list of keywords is not enough and the scene is described narratively; writing a prompt is about defining composition, lighting, aspect ratio, and emotional resonance, not just keywords. (models: pro, nb2)

title_en: Include subject, composition, action, location, style
content_en:
To achieve the best results and more nuanced creative control, include the following elements in the prompt:
1. Subject: who or what is in the image. Be specific.
2. Composition: how the shot is framed (e.g., extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait).
3. Action: what is happening.
4. Location: where the scene takes place.
5. Style: the overall aesthetic (e.g., 3D animation, film noir, watercolor painting, photorealistic, 1990s product photography).
6. Editing instructions (for modifying an existing image): be direct and specific.
applies_when_en: A from-scratch generation prompt is being written or assembled and its completeness is checked: the subject is named with features, what it does, where, how the shot is framed, in which style or medium; for an edit, an instruction on what exactly to change.
not_applies_when_en: An information image (infographic, diagram), where the format and content are key; an edit of one property; a short edit on an attached image, where the image itself provides the rest of the context; generation from a simple concept relying on the model's reasoning.

title_en: Ask for an image explicitly

If an image is needed, ask for it clearly in the request:
1. Describe the intent with phrases such as "create an image of" or "generate an image of".

title_en: Critical instructions first, question after context
content_en:

title_en: Ask explicitly for text and interleaved images
content_en:
1. The model can generate text as an image; to get text, ask for text output explicitly (e.g., "generate narrative text along with illustrations").
2. Text and images can be generated interleaved in one response, for example images for each step of a generated recipe, without separate requests to the model.
3. Ask in the prompt for both text and images for each step (e.g., an illustrated recipe with images created alongside the text as it is generated); this encourages interleaved output.
applies_when_en: A response of text and images is needed (step-by-step instruction, illustrated story, recipe) with images interleaved with text, several images in one request, or the text must come as text rather than as lettering in the image.
not_applies_when_en: One image without text is needed; the text must be drawn in the image.

Per-image constraints can go into the step request: "generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio", "Label each image with the step number but no other words." (models: pro, nb2, lite, nb25)
The model does not always follow the exact number of image outputs asked for. (models: unspecified)

caveats_en: Models are non-deterministic; a good result can take several attempts. (models: nb2)

title_en: Decompose and chain prompts
content_en:
Break prompts down into components:
1. Instead of many instructions in one prompt, create one prompt per instruction; the prompt to process can be chosen based on the user's input.
2. For complex tasks with multiple sequential steps, make each step a prompt and chain the prompts together in a sequence, so the output of one becomes the input of the next.
3. Aggregation: perform different parallel tasks on different portions of the data and aggregate the results to produce the final output.
applies_when_en: The task is multi-stage (first obtain or structure the data or script, then make images from it), or one prompt is overloaded with different instructions.
not_applies_when_en: One image with one clear task.

title_en: Agent asks for missing details once
content_en:
When an agent or text model composes the image prompt from the user's image description:
1. Compare the description with the ideal prompt: subject, environment, style, lighting, color and mood.
2. Ask the user for the missing details once per image instead of generating immediately; missing elements are acceptable if the user decides not to detail them.
3. Combine the original prompt with the responses and call generate_image.
4. Put into the generated prompt only the elements the user asked for, without examples.
applies_when_en: The image prompt is assembled by an agent or text model from the user's words, and the user's description is incomplete.
not_applies_when_en: The prompt is written directly for the image model without an intermediary.
forbids_in_output_en: DO NOT INCLUDE EXAMPLES IN THE GENERATED PROMPT
caveats_en: This is the system prompt of the orchestrator text model that composes prompts for the image model, not an instruction to the image model. (models: nb2, other)
Inside that system prompt the "no examples" line is a hard requirement (capitals); it keeps UI hint examples out of the image prompt. (models: nb2, other)
Sample prompts are short period-separated fragments covering one or two elements each, one with the aspect ratio appended. (models: nb2)

title_en: Best-performance prompt languages
content_en:
The image models support over 35 languages; the listed languages give the best performance:
1. Gemini 3.x Image models (pro, nb2, lite): ar-EG, de-DE, EN, es-MX, fr-FR, hi-IN, id-ID, it-IT, ja-JP, ko-KR, pt-BR, ru-RU, ua-UA, vi-VN, zh-CN.
2. Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (nb25): EN, es-MX, ja-JP, zh-CN, hi-IN.
applies_when_en: The prompt or the in-image text is not in English (for example, in Russian) or mixes languages; the prompt language must be chosen for a specific model.
not_applies_when_en: The product interface language; an English prompt without text in the image.
caveats_en: Vertex gives the 15 languages only for Gemini 3 Pro Image; extending the same list to NB2 and Lite rests only on Firebase ('Gemini 3.x Image models'). (models: pro, nb2, lite)
The code 'ua-UA' is as in the source (the standard ISO code for Ukrainian is uk). (models: pro)
'For best performance' is a recommendation; other languages are not forbidden. (models: nb25)
All Gemini models understand and answer in a list of languages (including Russian); whether this applies to text inside the image is not specified. (models: unspecified)
The list does not say whether it applies to the prompt language, in-image text, or both. (models: unspecified)
All Gemini models can understand and respond in about 100 listed languages including Russian; this is about understanding and answering, not in-image rendering. (models: unspecified)
The output language of in-image text can be requested in the prompt ("... in Spanish"). (models: nb2)

title_en: Docs visuals: action, format, content, placement
content_en: A document-aware visual prompt names the action (Visualize / Create / Generate), the visual format (infographic, timeline, flowchart, mind map), which content of the document to use, and where to insert the result in the document.
applies_when_en: In Google Docs, the content of a document must be turned into an infographic, a timeline, a flowchart or a mind map and inserted in the right place.
not_applies_when_en: The image is not related to the document content.
forbids_in_output_en: horizontal project timeline based on the dates in this document
caveats_en: The template is assembled from the four examples of the goal table and is not formulated explicitly; the placement part is present in three of the four examples (absent in the mind map). (models: unspecified)
The prompts point to the document content rather than retelling it. (models: unspecified)

title_en: Reference each attached input clearly
content_en: Handle multimodal inputs coherently: treat text, images, audio and video as equal-class inputs, and make the instructions clearly reference each modality as needed.
applies_when_en: Images or documents are attached to the prompt or there is a previous result, and the instruction must say which input each part refers to.
not_applies_when_en: Generation without inputs; a case where the subject's appearance must be changed (then the new state is described).
needs_from_prompt_en: the attached inputs (images, audio, video or documents) or a previous result
caveats_en: The rule comes from the general Gemini 3 guide; for images it is supported only by examples (extraction inferences), with no direct wording on image pages. (models: pro, nb25, unspecified)
